name: Is it worth building an ADU in Los Angeles if I only plan to rent it out—how good is the return on investment?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth building an ADU in Los Angeles if I only plan to rent it out—how good is the return on investment?

acceptedAnswer.text:
In many LA neighborhoods, a well-designed ADU can both increase property value and generate strong monthly rent, often improving overall cash flow and long‑term equity. The return depends heavily on your build cost, financing, and realistic rent for your area. 

Because ADUs add independent living space in a high-demand rental market, appraisers and buyers increasingly assign real value to them—not just “bonus space.”

Key factors:
- All‑in project cost vs market rent for similar ADUs nearby
- Financing terms (refi, HELOC, construction loan)
- Impact on overall property value and resale appeal
- Vacancy, management, utilities, and maintenance costs

Before you commit, run a simple pro forma: total project cost, new monthly payment, expected rent, and a few conservative scenarios. An experienced ADU builder who has seen appraisals and rent comps locally can sanity-check your assumptions so you’re not relying on best‑case numbers.
acceptedAnswer.description: In much of Los Angeles, ADUs can pencil out well as rentals because they add a full unit in a high‑demand market and usually boost property value. The ROI depends on build cost, financing, and realistic local rents, so run a conservative pro forma before you commit.
